_source: ANU Programs and Courses (programsandcourses.anu.edu.au) — program pages for the School of Computing's award programs.
_note: The Bachelor of Computing's 48-unit major requirement can be satisfied by one of the computing majors listed under each program's 'majors' array; the courses each major requires are in soco-majors.json, keyed by major code.

programs.title: Bachelor of Computing
requirements: 144 units total.
A minimum of 12 units must come from courses tagged Transdisciplinary Problem-Solving.
A minimum of 24 units must come from 3000- and 4000-level COMP courses.
A maximum of 60 units may come from 1000-level courses.
A minimum of 96 units from completion of courses from the following lists:
6 units from one of: COMP1100 Programming as Problem Solving, COMP1130 Programming as Problem Solving (Advanced).
6 units from one of: COMP1110 Structured Programming, COMP1140 Structured Programming (Advanced).
6 units from one of: MATH1005 Discrete Mathematical Models, MATH2222 Introduction to Mathematical Thinking: Problem-Solving and Proofs.
24 units from the compulsory courses: COMP1600 Foundations of Computing, COMP2100 Software Construction, COMP2300 Computer Architecture, COMP2400 Relational Databases.

48 units from courses in the subject area COMP Computer Science, OR completion of one of the computing majors: COMS-MAJ Computer Systems, CSEC-MAJ Cyber Security, DTSC-MAJ Data Science, HCCC-MAJ Human-Centred and Creative Computing, INFS-MAJ Information Systems, INSY-MAJ Intelligent Systems, SOFT-MAJ Software Development.

AND 6 units from an ICT-related list: ARTH2181, ASIA3032, DESN2010, ENGN1211, ENVS2015, INFS2024, INFS3002, INFS3024, MATH1013, MATH1115, MATH2301, MATH2307, MGMT2009, MUSI3309, SCOM3029, SOCY2038, SOCY2166, STAT1003, STAT1008.
A minimum of 48 units from elective courses offered by ANU.

A maximum of 60 units may come from completion of 1000-level courses
A minimum of 96 units from completion of courses from the following lists:

COMP1140 Structured Programming (Advanced) (6 units)

MATH1005 Discrete Mathematical Models (6 units)
MATH2222 Introduction to Mathematical Thinking: Problem-Solving and Proofs (6 units)

programs.title: Master of Computing
requirements: 96 units total.
A minimum of 24 units must come from 8000-level COMP courses.

30 units from the compulsory courses: COMP6120 Software Engineering, COMP6442 Software Construction, COMP7710 Structured Programming (12 units), COMP8280 Responsible Practice, Innovation and Leadership.
A minimum of 6 units from a foundational course: MATH6005 Discrete Mathematics Models, or COMP6260 Foundations of Computing.
A maximum of 12 units from project courses: COMP8715 Advanced Computing Team Project (must be completed twice, in consecutive semesters, 6+6 units), or COMP8830 Computing Internship (12 units).

24 units from completing one Specialisation: Artificial Intelligence, Computer Systems, Computational Foundations, Data Science, Human Centred and Creative Computing, Machine Learning, Software Development.
18 units from further 6000/7000/8000-level courses in the subject areas COMP Computer Science or ENGN Engineering.
6 units from elective courses offered by ANU.
